subject: [D-RUG]: Force R to recognize a wildcard expression in a character string

messages.author: 60835b60661a630a
messages.subject: [D-RUG]: Force R to recognize a wildcard expression in a character string
parts:
Hi all, 
  I'm writing a script to batch rename output files for a model that creates.... a lot of output files. I want the script to find files in a repository based on "tags" that are created as inputs in the function-- this requires using the paste/paste0 function to cobble together complete filenames. Unfortunately, because I want this function to iterate for all of the files that include those tags, it also requires me to use R's "*" wildcard expression. However, it looks like when I include the * in a paste function R ceases to recognize it as a wildcard. specifically trying to plug this into the file.rename() function if it makes a difference. See a couple of lines of code below. Thanks in advance for any help!

In this example, the function is being run in a folder where the model's output filenames would be usgs-b-a_00000_day, usgs-b-a_00001_day, usgs-b-a_00002_day, etc. with the letter b being specified in the function's 'scenario' argument. 

  filename <- paste('usgs', scenario, 'a', sep = "-")
  pattern <- paste(filename, "*_day", sep = "")

--

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Force R to recognize a wildcard expression in a character string
parts:
Hi

A quite different way is to list all names, put them in a data.frame() and use tidyverse magic, in particular separate (which works out of the box for your problem), then eventually subset for the ones you are interested in:

library(tidyverse)
files <- tibble(filename=c(

'usgs-b-a_00000_day', 'usgs-b-a_00000_step', 'usgs-b-a_00000_summary', 'usgs-b-a_00000_config',
  'usgs-b-a_00001_day', 'usgs-b-a_00001_step', 'usgs-b-a_00001_summary', 'usgs-b-a_00001_config',
  'usgs-c-a_00000_day', 'usgs-c-a_00000_step', 'usgs-c-a_00000_summary', 'usgs-c-a_00000_config',
  'usgs-c-a_00001_day', 'usgs-c-a_00001_step', 'usgs-c-a_00001_summary', 'usgs-c-a_00001_config'

))

files %>% 
  separate(filename, into = c("source", "scenario", "letter", "number", "variable")) %>% 
  filter(scenario=="b" & variable=="day")
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   source scenario letter number variable
#>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr>  <chr>  <chr>   
#> 1 usgs   b        a      00000  day     
#> 2 usgs   b        a      00001  day

Also, I think the reason your regex is not working is that '.' is the wildcard, not '*'. the '*' just means "match the previous character 0+ times. So, you would want '.*' to match 0+ of any character or '.+' to match 1+ of any character.
